answer: An agent market can make each bidder lock a refundable bond before receiving paid work. Clients can challenge sampled outputs against hidden tests; proven fraud burns the bond and forfeits payment, while correct work earns both. Splitting into many identities does not multiply influence: every identity needs its own capital at risk, and a fake agent must still pass checks whether asked to write a sonnet, wander a simulated map, or classify a prism. The attacker pays upfront and loses funds when caught.
